findings.title: E-1 tasks are proved by tests that need commands and helpers from tasks that depend on them
quotes: - Test: TC-6, TC-7, TC-9, TC-58, TC-59, TC-73, TC-74, TC-75
### T-6 The test helpers `effort`, `history`, `cli`, `snap` in tests/test_flow.py, and `flow.pick` / `flow.kind` (CT-4)
findings.fix: give T-1, T-2 and T-4 only the tests their own code can pass, or new unit TCs that call `load`, `record`, `lock` and `guard` directly. Move TC-6, TC-12, TC-13 to TC-16 and TC-56 to T-8, T-9 and T-12, where most of them already appear. Or move T-6's helpers ahead of E-1 and make T-1, T-2 and T-4 depend on it, adding `tests/test_flow.py` to their Files.

sources.situation: a worker gets T-1 with Files `src/nio/flow.py` only. TC-6 calls `flow.start` (built in T-8, which depends on T-1) and the `effort` helper (built in T-6, which depends on T-1). TC-74 and TC-75 call `flow.park` (T-9). The test can't be written in a file the task doesn't list, and it can't pass. The same holds for T-2: TC-12 and TC-56 run `cli(root, "park", ...)`, and `park` comes in T-9. It holds for T-4 too: TC-13 to TC-16 call `flow.done`, which comes in T-12. Each worker either stops or invents an untested stub, and nothing proves the task is done.

findings.reason: T-1's Test lists TC-6 (calls `flow.start`, built in T-8, and the `effort` helper from T-6) and TC-74/75 (call `flow.park`, T-9), but its Files are only `src/nio/flow.py`. T-2 (TC-12, TC-56 run `park`) and T-4 (TC-13 to TC-16 call `flow.done`, T-12) have the same problem. Nothing in tests.md or tasks.md lets those tests pass at that point.
findings.note: T-6 (helpers) moved first; T-1, T-2, T-3, T-4 depend on it, list tests/test_flow.py and test their own code directly; command-level tests named as proved later by T-8, T-9, T-10, T-12, T-13, T-16, T-19

findings.title: T-5's test runs `start` and `next`, which come later and depend on T-5
findings.fix: give T-5 only TC-77, plus a test that a stub `ValueError`, `Broken` or `Busy` prints `error: ...` and exits 1, and add `tests/test_flow.py` to its Files. TC-3 already sits in T-8, and TC-12 already sits in T-9.

sources.situation: T-5 builds only the argparse wiring. TC-3 needs `flow.start` (T-8, which depends on T-5) and `flow.next_step` (T-7). TC-12 needs `park` (T-9). The `cli` helper comes from T-6. So T-5's tests fail whatever the worker does, and its Files list no test file.

findings.reason: T-5's Test lists TC-3, which runs `cli(root,"start",...)` then `next`. `start` is T-8, which depends on T-5, and `next` is T-7. TC-12 needs `park` (T-9), and T-5's Files list no test file.
findings.note: T-5 tests only TC-77 plus the error-to-exit-1 check, with tests/test_flow.py and T-6

findings.title: T-11 runs in parallel while writing to the test file E-2 is building
findings.fix: set T-11 to `Parallel: no` and make it depend on T-6. Or put TC-11 in its own test file so T-11 shares no file with E-2.

sources.situation: T-11 depends on nothing and runs alongside T-6 to T-10, and all of them edit tests/test_flow.py. T-6 creates the module's helpers and test layout while T-11 adds `test_ac11_no_hand_edit_instruction` to the same file. That file already holds the 4 waiting #42 tests. Two workers' edits then collide or overwrite each other, depending on which one lands first.

findings.reason: T-11 has `Depends on: none` and `Parallel: yes`, and its Files include `tests/test_flow.py`. T-6 to T-10 also edit that file, and T-6 creates its helpers. Nothing orders T-11 against them, so the shared-file collision is real.
findings.note: T-11 is Parallel: no and depends on T-6

findings.title: T-7's line-limit test needs unseen overrides, which come from tasks it doesn't depend on
quotes: the planning one with 5 unseen overrides.
findings.fix: move TC-65 to T-20, which adds unseen overrides to `next`, or add TC-65 to T-20's Test as well and drop the override part from T-7's run.

sources.situation: TC-65 builds a planning effort with 5 unseen overrides and checks that `next` stays within 12 lines. Overrides and the unseen flag come from T-19 and T-20, which run after T-7. A worker on T-7 can't build that setup, and `next` doesn't print overrides yet. So TC-65 either can't run, or passes without testing the overrides part of NFR-1.

findings.reason: T-7's Test includes TC-65, whose setup is a planning effort with 5 unseen overrides. Overrides come from T-19 and the unseen flag from T-20, and T-7 depends only on T-4 and T-6. The override part of TC-65 can't be built at T-7.
findings.note: TC-65 moved to T-20; T-7 names it as proved later by T-20

findings.title: T-6 now runs first but is still proved by TC-4, which needs `nio flow next` from T-7 and T-5
quotes: Given no current effort and no slug, when `nio flow next` runs, then it fails and lists the efforts it could start.
- Test: TC-1, TC-2, TC-4, TC-8; TC-65 proved later by T-20, which adds unseen overrides to `next`
findings.fix: drop TC-4 from T-6's Test and Serves, since T-7 already proves it. Give T-6 direct unit checks on `flow.pick` and `flow.kind` (no current effort, a legacy folder, an intake-only folder) and on the helpers it builds, and note "TC-4 proved later by T-7".

sources.situation: a worker gets T-6, the first task, with nothing before it. TC-4 runs `nio flow next` with no slug and expects it to fail and list the efforts it could start. `flow.next_step` comes from T-7 and the `next` subparser from T-5, and both depend on T-6. TC-4 can't pass. The worker either stops or writes a stub `next` that T-7 and T-5 later replace, and nothing proves T-6 is done. T-7 already lists TC-4.

findings.reason: tests.md TC-4 is a unit test whose Action is `flow.pick(root)`, not `nio flow next`. It asserts a `ValueError` naming the efforts and `nio flow start`, and it covers CT-4. T-6's title (tasks.md) builds `flow.pick` / `flow.kind (CT-4)` with Depends on: none, so T-6 can pass TC-4 on its own. The finding took the AC-4 sentence "when `nio flow next` runs" as the test action. T-7 also lists TC-4, but that is extra coverage and does not stop T-6 from proving it.
